resale_co.name: Resale Certificate of Occupancy (Resale Inspection)
resale_co.issued_by: Monroe Township Housing Office (Housing Official Dan Kozak)
resale_co.lead_time: Submit the application 3 to 4 weeks before settlement. Requests with less than 7 business days cost more.
resale_co.valid_for: Inspections are only valid for 60 days
requirements: House numbers at least 3 inches on both sides of the mailbox
Smoke alarms on all levels; battery alarms must be 10-year sealed units; hardwired alarms must stay hardwired and be under 10 years old
Carbon monoxide alarms outside sleeping areas (exception for all-electric homes with detached garages)

Fire extinguisher 2A-10B:C, no more than 10 lb, mounted with its bracket within 10 ft of the kitchen in the exit path, top no higher than 5 ft, serviced and tagged within 12 months or new with receipt, manual left for new occupant
Satisfactory lab report including mercury for private wells
Satisfactory septic certification from Gloucester County Dept of Health for private septic
Exterior clean, safe and in satisfactory condition
Pool barriers: 4 ft fence and self-closing, self-latching gate that opens out with release 54 inches from the ground; no stagnant water
Hot tub safety straps in good working order
Abandoned property registration fees and emergency work charges paid
All zoning, construction and Board of Health permits and violations closed and penalties paid
All property maintenance violations satisfied and penalties paid
Buyer's notarized Acknowledgement of Responsibility form submitted with the application

resale_co.how_to_apply: Download the Resale Application Packet, fill out the application, and have the buyer sign the Acknowledgement of Responsibility in front of a notary (the original is required; inspections cannot be scheduled without it). Submit in person or by mail to the Monroe Township Housing Office, 125 Virginia Avenue, Williamstown, NJ 08094, with exact cash, check or money order payable to 'Monroe Township Housing'. No credit or debit cards. All fees are non-refundable. For as-is sales, include the contract cover sheet and the clause making the buyer responsible for certificates and inspections.

evidence.quote: Resale Inspections take place at the change of each ownership for dwellings in Monroe Township, and the application can be found on the Township website in the forms section. An inspection shall be performed prior to the change of ownership, and a Certificate of Occupancy will be issued following a passing inspection.
** INSPECTIONS ARE ONLY VALID FOR 60 DAYS.** ... APPLICATIONS SHOULD BE SUBMITTED 3-4 WEEKS BEFORE SETTLEMENT.
ALL CONSTRUCTION PERMITS AND VIOLATIONS MUST BE CLOSED PRIOR TO CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY BEING ISSUED

resale_co.notes: Packet revised 8/3/26 adds a required notarized buyer 'Acknowledgement of Responsibility' under Township Code section 162-11.S. As-is sales: if the inspection fails, the buyer can sign a notarized affidavit taking responsibility for the failed items, which allows a 'Certificate of Transfer Ownership only with No Occupancy' and covers the reinspection for the CO once repairs are done. The township also strongly recommends the buyer get a survey no more than 90 days old and file an OPRA request for zoning and construction permits (including Pinelands approvals). Rentals have a separate annual registration and change-of-tenant inspection.

requirements: The township resale checklist says all battery smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed units (effective Jan 1, 2019), hardwired alarms must stay hardwired and be under 10 years old, and the extinguisher must be serviced and tagged by a certified contractor within 12 months or be new with a receipt, weigh no more than 10 lb, and be mounted with the top no more than 5 ft above the floor

authorities.name: Monroe Township Bureau of Fire Prevention (Department of Public Safety)
authorities.area_served: Entire township (covers both the Williamstown and Cecil fire company areas)
authorities.how_to_apply: Contact the Bureau of Fire Prevention. The smoke alarm, CO alarm and extinguisher items are also checked as part of the Housing Office resale CO inspection; the township does not say whether a separate Bureau certificate or fee is needed.

evidence.quote: We work along with the following departments to enforce the related ordinances in the Codes of the Township of Monroe: Williamstown and Cecil Fire Departments, Construction Department, Zoning, Planning Board Department, Emergency Management and Department of Community Affairs.
EFFECTIVE JANUARY 1, 2019, ALL BATTERY SMOKE DETECTORS MUST BE 10 YEAR SEALED BATTERY UNITS.

fire_cert.notes: DCA LEA Registry (July 2026) lists Monroe Township, Gloucester County as 'M' (the municipality is the local enforcing agency), with no separate district LEAs for this Monroe. (The 'D Monroe Township (1), (2), (3)' entries in the registry are Monroe Township in Middlesex County.) Monroe (Gloucester) has two fire companies, Williamstown and Cecil, but no evidence was found that either acts as the smoke certificate authority, so one township-wide authority is listed. Fire Official named on the 2024 fire permit form: Patrick K. Mason; Fire Marshal email firemarshal@monroetownshipnj.org. No published resale smoke certificate fee was found.

other_items.label: Open permits and violations must be closed
other_items.detail: All construction permits and violations must be closed before the CO is issued; all zoning, construction, Board of Health and property maintenance violations satisfied and penalties paid.

other_items.label: Private well test
other_items.detail: Satisfactory lab report including mercury for private wells.

other_items.label: Septic certification
other_items.detail: Satisfactory septic certification for private septic systems by Gloucester County Dept of Health.

other_items.label: Abandoned property fees and emergency work charges
other_items.detail: Must be paid in full before the CO.

other_items.label: Buyer Acknowledgement of Responsibility (notarized)
other_items.detail: Original notarized form completed by the buyer must be submitted with the application; the CO can be denied without it.

open_questions: Whether the Bureau of Fire Prevention issues a separate smoke/CO/extinguisher certificate (and fee) on resale, or whether the Housing Office resale CO inspection serves as the certificate, is not stated on official pages.
Some linked township PDFs (Helpful Guide to Permits and Certificates, Rental Fees and Requirements, Ordinances O-48-2024 and O-49-2024) returned web pages instead of PDFs and could not be read.
